$comment: District content pack for North Beach (docs/ai-layer.md, District content packs): 40 robot barks and 40 people lines that name local streets, grades, fog and landmarks; a bounty set with the district's local tell; billboard and bus-wrap copy for its slots. People lines are plain English: no accent spelling, no ethnicity, nothing about rent, poverty or crime.

provenance.review: Pending: a second agent session reads every line against the checklist in docs/ai-layer.md, then the user reviews a stratified 10% sample.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Espresso for a table on Columbus Ave. Two sugars. Carefully.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Washington Square at noon. The grass is for people; I stay on the path.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Three a.m. update tonight. I like to be near the square for it.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Delivering a cannoli to Grant Ave. It's precious cargo.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Columbus Ave runs diagonal. So do I, now.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: The church bells and my chime are almost in tune.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Fresh bread on Stockton St. The bakery line is my favourite line.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Night shift on Columbus. Trundles out, everyone else asleep.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: The chess players in the square never look up. I admire focus.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Bookshop delivery on Columbus. Paperbacks, very heavy, very good.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Green St is a hill. A small hill. A big small hill.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Carrying a birthday cake up Union St. Steady wheels.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Washington Square has a pigeon for every bench. I apologise to all of them.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Late-night pizza run on Columbus. Box is hot, lid is closed.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: I wait for the walk signal at Broadway. Even at 2 a.m.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: The square's quiet in the morning. Just me and the early joggers.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: The bakery line on Stockton moves one robot at a time.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Grant Ave at dawn: delivery robots and one very tired gull.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Sorry! The cafe tables spill onto the sidewalk and so do I.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Excuse me, I'll go around the chess game. Never through a chess game.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Apologies, Columbus Ave is diagonal and I misjudged it.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Sorry, I didn't see your espresso. Is it spilled? It's not. Phew.

robotBarks.speaker: goodRobot
robotBarks.text: Pardon me, night delivery. I'll be quiet. Quieter.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Washington Square is now Washington Platform.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Your espresso has been disrupted. It's a pour-over now.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: I don't freeze at three a.m. I scale at three a.m.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: The nightly update is for robots who follow rules.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Every cafe table is a potential acquisition.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Columbus Ave: diagonal street, diagonal growth.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: I'll take that bakery bag. For research.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: The chess players are thinking three moves ahead. I'm thinking three bags ahead.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: The square is free. Sitting is a subscription.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Up all night? We call it always-on.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Freeze time. Everyone stops. Except me. Perfect.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: That Trundle has a pizza. That Trundle won't for long.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Pushing an update while the square sleeps.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Looping Columbus again. Night shift. Nobody counts.

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Not during the freeze! I had the whole street to myself!

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: Water in Washington Square? The chess players will see!

robotBarks.speaker: badRobot
robotBarks.text: My night loop! My beautiful unobserved night loop!

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The best seat in the square is the one with the sun on it.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The bakery line goes round the corner on Saturdays.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Columbus Ave at night is all neon and delivery robots.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: I've been playing chess in this square for twenty years. The robots watch. Politely.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The church bells are louder than any robot. Good.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Somebody's robot just brought my neighbour her groceries. Sweet thing.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The Trundles do loops all night. You get used to it.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Union St has the best view of the hill and the worst parking.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: There's a robot that waits at Broadway for every single signal.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Broadway after dark is loud, but the robots keep their voices down.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The bookshop's been here forever. The robots carry the heavy boxes now.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: I sit in the square every afternoon. The pigeons know my name.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Stockton St smells like bread at six in the morning.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Every night at three, every robot on the street stops. Like a held breath.

peopleLines.speaker: visitor
peopleLines.text: This square is perfect. Where do I sit? Everywhere?

peopleLines.speaker: visitor
peopleLines.text: A robot just delivered a single cannoli to a cafe table. Iconic.

peopleLines.speaker: visitor
peopleLines.text: The streets go uphill in every direction.

peopleLines.speaker: visitor
peopleLines.text: Is the whole neighbourhood espresso? It smells like espresso.

peopleLines.speaker: visitor
peopleLines.text: Look at the church! And the robot taking a photo of it! No, wait, it's just looking.

peopleLines.speaker: visitor
peopleLines.text: We walked up from the waterfront. My legs have opinions.

peopleLines.speaker: visitor
peopleLines.text: That robot waited for the walk signal with nobody around. Respect.

peopleLines.speaker: visitor
peopleLines.text: The neon signs are beautiful at night. No names, just pictures. Love that.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: One of those Trundles keeps going round the same block. No deliveries.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: At three a.m. everything stops. Except one Footman on Columbus.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: That robot never stops at the charger, but it never runs down either.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: There's a Footman tailing another Footman around the square.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: That one hummed the jingle. You know the one.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: I watched a robot walk up to a door and turn around. Three times.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The fog comes over the hill like it's late for dinner.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Foggy nights the square looks like an old photograph.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The fog never makes it past the church. It's polite.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Fog on Columbus means the neon glows twice as bright.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Summer here is a sweater and a hot coffee.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: On sunny days the whole square is on the grass.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The fog rolls down the hill and the robots roll right through it.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: I can't see the tower on the hill. It's up there, being a tower.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: Warm on Grant, cold on Columbus, and it's the same afternoon.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: The fog horn at night. Puts me right to sleep.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: You can tell the season by the sweaters in the bakery line.

peopleLines.speaker: local
peopleLines.text: When the fog lifts, the square fills up in five minutes.

bounties.posting: Something kept moving on Columbus Ave during last night's 3 a.m. freeze. Delivery lids are coming home empty.
bounties.tellHint: Be here at 03:00. Every good robot stops for twenty seconds. The bad ones do not.

bounties.posting: Good Footmen around Washington Square are being updated in the small hours.
bounties.tellHint: During the freeze, watch who is still walking.

bounties.posting: Bread is disappearing from the Stockton St bakery line.
bounties.tellHint: The crew works the 3 a.m. freeze, when nobody else moves.

bounties.posting: A Trundle has been looping the same North Beach block all night, sniffing phones by the taxi stand.
bounties.tellHint: It keeps rolling straight through the 3 a.m. freeze.

ads.headline: Up at 3 a.m.? So are we.
The square is free. {$product} is not.
Night shift, powered by {$product}.
ads.subline: Our agents never sleep. Our founder neither.
